title: Astra for Law leads one legal test. Most assignments still fail it.
friendlyTitle: A legal ChatGPT setup leads one test. Most tasks still fail it.
summary: On 17 November, OpenAI said every ChatGPT Enterprise customer can request Astra for Law, a GPT-6.2 Astra setup with a larger legal search index. Teams that already have it select gpt-6.2-astra-law. On Harvey's LAB-AA test, as presented by OpenAI, it earned full credit on 20.8% of 120 assignments, ahead of plain GPT-6.2 Astra at 15.0%.
friendlySummary: On 17 November, OpenAI said every ChatGPT Enterprise customer can ask for Astra for Law. It is the new Astra model plus a larger legal search index. On one legal test, OpenAI says it fully passed 20.8% of 120 tasks. The same model without the legal setup fully passed 15.0%.
whyItMatters: Full credit means every requirement was met and no material claim was invented. Most assignments still missed that bar. OpenAI also cites 0.03 material hallucinations per assignment, against 0.59 for Claude Opus 5.5, on Artificial Analysis's comparison. A brief is not filed until a lawyer checks the citations.
friendlyWhyItMatters: A full pass means every requirement was met and no important claim was invented. Most tasks still missed that bar. OpenAI also cites fewer invented claims than another leading model on that comparison. A legal brief is not filed until a lawyer checks the citations.
